Despite this massive over-parameterization and explicit training on lengths up to L = 50 L=50 , the model failed to capture the underlying rule. While it achieved perfect accuracy on short sequences, it exhibited failure as lengths increased, collapsing to random guessing ( ≈ 10 % \approx 10\% ). This indicates a failure of combinatorial generalization: despite seeing examples of these lengths during training, the model failed to learn the algebraic rule required to handle the exponentially growing state space, relying instead on fragile positional heuristics. While modern relative positional encodings (e.g., RoPE [ 29 ] , ALiBi [ 30 ] ) improve local extrapolation, they remain fundamentally metric and are applied within a commutative attention mechanism—encoding order via geometric rotation or decay. Consequently, empirical studies confirm they typically degrade beyond 2 – 4 × 2\text{--}4\times the training window [ 37 ] , failing to support the order-of-magnitude ( 100 × 100\times ) generalization demonstrated here. Furthermore, the Transformer’s computational cost scales quadratically O ​ ( L 2 ) O(L^{2}) with context, making it physically energetically unfavorable for long-horizon inference.
